subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should the public `openclaw cron run` contract become permanently non-consuming for deleteAfterRun jobs and scheduler-owned counters, with consumption reserved for timer and gateway on-exit execution?
rationale: The change intentionally alters an existing operator-visible behavior and persists an attribution field; source review can establish consistency but cannot decide whether compatibility with workflows that manually consume a one-shot should be retained.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming manual runs
options.body: Confirm that public manual runs are verification-only and require final-head runtime proof before merging.

options.title: Preserve an explicit consuming operator path
options.body: Keep the current behavior available behind a separately designed, documented operator-only command or flag if intentional manual consumption remains supported.

options.title: Pause for narrower contract design
options.body: Defer the behavioral change until maintainers define manual-run semantics across CLI, RPC, and automation callers.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming manual runs
recommendation.body: Confirm that public manual runs are verification-only and require final-head runtime proof before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the adjacent cron scheduling and pending-slot invariants that this contract changes.
